User: I'm going through a legal process and need to organize my thoughts. The case involves nondisclosure agreement dispute. My lawyer is Lisa Park with Park Legal Group; we have proceedings at the federal district court. We're past the filing stage and waiting for the court calendar.. Opposing party: my former landlord. This is in King County, Washington. The contract was signed last year and they've since stopped performing. Can you help me figure out what to ask my attorney about what documents I should bring and what to say in the hearing? I want to be ready for the legal next steps.
Assistant: I can help you get organized. I’m not a lawyer, but below are practical, attorney-focused questions to ask Lisa Park, a detailed documents checklist to gather, a short “what to say” script you can use at the hearing, and other prep tips. If you want, I can also draft a concise email to Lisa requesting guidance and attaching your documents/timeline.

1) First — confirm with your attorney
- Ask what kind of hearing it will be (status conference, motion hearing, calendar call, preliminary injunction, evidentiary hearing, settlement conference, etc.). The type of hearing changes what to prepare.
- Ask whether any filings (exhibit lists, witness lists, proposed orders, declarations, exhibits) are required in advance and the deadlines for each.
- Ask whether any documents should be filed under seal (since this involves an NDA) and the court’s sealing procedure.
- Ask whether you should appear in person or if remote appearance is permitted/expected, and logistics (arrival time, courtroom number, length estimate).

2) Key questions to ask Lisa Park (so you cover strategy and practicalities)
- What specifically will the court be asked to decide at this hearing?
- What is our objective at the hearing (scheduling only, get a ruling on a motion, obtain injunctive relief, preserve evidence, etc.)?
- Which documents do you want me to bring/prepare as exhibits or declarations?
- Do you want me to prepare a sworn declaration/affidavit? If so, what facts should it include and how should it be organized?
- Are there specific witnesses we should present or affidavits from third parties?
- How should we present confidential materials (redaction, sealing motion, in-camera review)?
- What questions should I expect from opposing counsel or the judge — and what are good, short answers?
- How should I testify if called — what are the “don’ts” (e.g., don’t volunteer extra info, answer only what’s asked)?
- Do we have to bring originals or are copies sufficient? How many copies for the court and opposing counsel?
- Do you recommend any last-minute discovery or preservation steps (e.g., preserve emails, metadata, devices)?
- What settlement posture should I take? Any settlement range to authorize or not to exceed?
- What are the next steps after this hearing and likely timeline (discovery schedule, summary judgment deadlines, trial estimate)?

3) Documents to gather and bring (organize in a tabbed binder or a well-labeled PDF folder)
Core contract and identity documents
- The signed NDA (original if you have it; copy is fine if original not available).
- Any related contracts or amendments (leases, addenda, rider, side agreements).
- Proof of signature/date (if available).

Communications & performance evidence
- All communications with the landlord about the NDA and performance: emails, text messages, letters, messages (with dates/time).
- Any written notices you gave or received (notices of breach, cure notices, termination letters).
- Records showing your compliance or performance under the contract (receipts, logs, deliveries, effort records).
- Any communication that shows the landlord stopped performing (promises, cancellations, refusals).

Financial/damage evidence
- Invoices, receipts, cancelled checks, bank statements, payment records showing damages or expenses you incurred because of their non-performance.
- If claiming lost opportunity or other quantifiable damages, supporting documents (estimates, invoices, expert reports if any).

Chronology/timeline
- A one-page timeline of key dates (contract date, performance milestones, dates landlord stopped performing, notice dates, filings).
- A short factual summary (2–3 paragraphs) of the dispute for the attorney and for the judge (if needed).

Court and case documents
- All filed pleadings and court orders (complaint, answer, briefs, motions, proof of service, docket report).
- Any discovery responses, interrogatories, production logs you’ve already exchanged.
- Any prior hearing transcripts or orders.

Evidence authenticity & technical
- Originals or verifiable copies; if relying on electronic evidence, preserve originals and metadata (email headers, timestamps).
- Witness contact info and short written statements or declarations (if available).
- Any photos, screenshots, or recordings relevant to the dispute.

Practical items
- Your ID, case number, counsel contact details, directions to courthouse, parking info.
- Several paper copies of key exhibits (ask Lisa how many copies to bring).

4) What to say at the hearing — short script and tips
- Keep it short and factual. If Lisa speaks for you, you’ll likely only need brief confirmations or to answer direct questions.
- Opening lines (if you need to speak or the judge asks you to state your position):
  “Good morning, Your Honor. I’m [Your Name], the plaintiff (or defendant). We’re here for [type of hearing]. My counsel is Lisa Park of Park Legal Group. Briefly, this case concerns [one-sentence description: e.g., enforcement for breach of an NDA entered on DATE where the landlord stopped performing obligations]. We ask the Court to [state the relief sought for this hearing: e.g., set a discovery schedule / rule on the pending motion / set a hearing date / grant preliminary relief].”
- If asked factual questions, answer succinctly with dates and short facts. Example:
  Q: “When did they stop performing?” A: “On [date]. On that date they [specific action or failure]. I have emails showing that [cite exhibit number].”
- Don’t speculate, don’t volunteer extra background, and say “I don’t recall” rather than guessing if unsure.
- If a legal or strategic question arises, defer: “My counsel can address the legal issues; I can provide factual background.”

5) Prepare a one-page facts/timeline and a one-line objective
- Create a single sheet that contains:
  - Case caption, case number, judge, hearing date.
  - One-line statement of remedy sought for this hearing.
  - Ten-line timeline of critical dates.
  - Three bullet “key facts” you want the judge to know.
- Give this to Lisa in advance and bring a printed copy to court.

6) Evidence and admissibility
- Ask Lisa which documents need authentication and whether she will file declarations (your sworn declaration can authenticate documents).
- Ask whether any documents should be pre-marked as exhibits and if a joint exhibit list is needed.

7) Courtroom behavior and logistics
- Dress conservatively and arrive early (plan for security screening).
- Turn off cell phones. Bring only necessary documents.
- Speak clearly, stand when addressing the judge, look at the judge when speaking.
- If remote, test your connection and have documents ready to share.

8) Preservation steps you should confirm now
- Preserve all relevant communications (emails, texts, voicemails) and devices — do not delete anything.
- If anything has been destroyed or altered, tell your attorney immediately.

9) Settlement and strategy
- Ask if settlement communications should continue or be paused, and whether anything you say to the opposing party could hurt litigation.
- Ask whether to authorize Lisa to accept settlement within a range or if all offers must be cleared with you.

10) Offer from me
- I can draft:
  - A concise email to Lisa Park summarizing these items and asking for her checklist and deadlines.
  - Your one-page timeline/fact sheet if you give me the key dates and short facts.
  - A short script you can practice for likely questions.

Next step for me (if you want)
- Tell me whether you want me to draft the email to Lisa Park and provide:
  - Case number and judge (if known)
  - Any key dates and brief timeline
  - Your preferred settlement authority (if any)
- Or paste the key dates/facts and I’ll produce a one-page timeline and a short hearing script you can rehearse.

Would you like me to draft the email to Lisa Park now or prepare your one-page timeline from the facts you provided?
